fields.title: The Revelation to John
fields.subtitle: Apokalypsis Iōannou, “The Revelation of John”
fields.description: The last book of the Bible, a vision given to John in exile on Patmos and sent to seven churches in Asia, with a blessing on everyone who reads it aloud and everyone who listens. The risen Christ among the lampstands and his letters to the churches; the throne in heaven, and the Lion of Judah who turns out to be a Lamb that was slaughtered; seals, trumpets and bowls; the dragon, the beast and the fall of Babylon the great; the rider called the Word of God; the thousand years and the great white throne; and a new heaven and a new earth, where God wipes every tear from their eyes and makes everything new. In the Open Word Bible, a new translation from the Greek given freely to the public domain, with an introduction to the book’s shape and meaning and a conclusion on where to read next.

qa.question: What is the book of Revelation?
qa.answer: The twenty-seventh and last book of the New Testament, an account of visions given to a prophet named John. It is at once an apocalypse, a book of symbolic visions like Daniel; a prophecy; and a letter to seven churches in the Roman province of Asia. It shows the risen Jesus, the worship of heaven, God’s judgments on evil, the fall of the powers that oppose him, and a new heaven and a new earth. Its name comes from its first word in Greek, apokalypsis, an unveiling.

qa.question: Who wrote Revelation, and when?
qa.answer: The writer calls himself John and says he was on the island of Patmos “because of God’s word and the testimony of Jesus” (1:9). From the second century most of the church identified him with John the apostle; Dionysius of Alexandria in the third century argued from its very different Greek that it was another John, and many scholars today agree. Irenaeus dates the vision toward the end of the emperor Domitian’s reign, around AD 95, the date most scholars accept; some date it to the late 60s, after Nero’s persecution.

qa.question: What is the meaning of the Lamb in Revelation?
qa.answer: In chapter 5 John is told that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has overcome and can open the sealed scroll, but when he looks he sees “a Lamb standing, looking as though he had been slaughtered” (5:6). The image shows that Jesus, Israel’s promised King, has conquered through his death. From then on Revelation calls him the Lamb nearly thirty times, and all creation worships him, singing that he is worthy because by his blood he bought for God people from every nation.

qa.question: What is the number of the beast, 666?
qa.answer: In 13:18 John invites whoever has understanding to count up the number of the beast, “for it is a human number. Its number is 666.” Many scholars think the first readers would have heard in it the name of the emperor Nero, whose name in Hebrew letters adds up to 666; a few early manuscripts read 616, which fits the same name spelled from its Latin form. Others take it as a symbol of human power that always falls short of seven, the number of completeness. Irenaeus warned in the second century that the number can be fitted to many names.

qa.question: What are the main ways Christians interpret Revelation and the thousand years?
qa.answer: Preterists read Revelation chiefly as about John’s own time and the struggle with Rome; historicists as a survey of church history; futurists as describing events still to come before Christ’s return; idealists as a picture of the conflict between God and evil in every age. On the thousand years of chapter 20, premillennialists expect Christ to return and then reign on earth, amillennialists, following Augustine, take it as the present age of the church, and postmillennialists expect a long triumph of the gospel before he comes. All agree that Christ will return, the dead will be raised, and God will make all things new.

qa.answer: The Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Greek and dedicated to the public domain, printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. It gives distances and measures in modern units, with the original measures available in the Open Word Bible itself. The reasoning behind each of its sentences, with the Greek beside it, is published at openwordbible.org. The introduction and conclusion were written for this edition.

fields.title: Introduction
fields.body_html:
How blessed is the one who reads the words of this prophecy aloud, and those who hear them and keep what is written here! The time is near.

— Revelation 1:3

No book of the Bible has been more feared, more avoided, or more argued over than Revelation. It has been used to frighten people, to calculate the end of the world, and to put names to the beast; and many Christians, weary of all that, have simply left it closed. Yet it is the only book of the Bible that begins by promising a blessing to the person who reads it aloud and to those who listen. It was written to be heard in church, from beginning to end, by ordinary believers. It expected them to understand it, and to be strengthened by it.

The key is in the first words: “This is the revelation of Jesus Christ.” The Greek word is apokalypsis, an unveiling, the pulling back of a curtain. Revelation is not a book of riddles meant to hide the future. It is a book of pictures meant to show the present as heaven sees it: who truly rules the world, what the powers of the age really are, and how the story ends. Above all it is a revelation of Jesus himself, the one who was dead and is alive for all the ages to come.

A vision, a prophecy and a letter

Revelation is three kinds of writing at once. It is an apocalypse, a vision full of symbols, of a kind well known in Jewish writing of the time, with the book of Daniel as its great model. It is a prophecy, as John calls it in 1:3, a word from God to his people about their own day as well as the days to come. And it is a letter: “From John, to the seven churches in the province of Asia” (1:4), with a greeting of grace and peace like any letter of Paul.

Each matters. Because it is an apocalypse, its images are meant to be seen and felt rather than decoded one by one, as a political cartoon is read as a whole rather than line by line. Because it is a prophecy, it speaks with God’s authority and calls for a response. Because it is a letter, it was written to real churches in real cities, and whatever else it means, it must have meant something to them.

John on Patmos

I, John, am your brother, and in Jesus I share with you the affliction, the kingdom, and the endurance. It was because of God’s word and the testimony of Jesus that I came to be on the island called Patmos.

— Revelation 1:9

Patmos is a small rocky island off the coast of what is now Turkey. John was there, it seems, in exile, as a punishment for his preaching. “On the Lord’s day I came to be in the Spirit”, he writes (1:10), and behind him he heard a voice like a trumpet.

Irenaeus, writing around AD 180, says the vision was seen “towards the end of Domitian’s reign”, that is, in the mid-90s, and most scholars still date it then. Others date it to the late 60s, after Nero’s persecution of the Christians in Rome. The writer calls himself simply John, a servant and a brother. From the second century most of the church identified him with John the apostle. But Dionysius, bishop of Alexandria in the third century, noticed how different the Greek of Revelation is from that of the Gospel and letters of John, and thought it the work of another John, a holy and inspired man; many scholars today agree. Either way, he writes as a prophet known to the churches of Asia, sharing their troubles and their hope.

The one like a son of man

The first thing John sees is not a beast or a battle but Jesus, standing among seven gold lampstands, which are the seven churches. He is “one like a son of man”, the figure of Daniel 7, with hair white as snow, eyes like flaming fire, and a face as bright as the sun. John falls at his feet like a dead man:

At the sight of him I fell down at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me and said, “Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last and the one who lives. I was dead, and see, I am alive for all the ages to come, and the keys of death and Hades are mine.

— Revelation 1:17–18

That is how the book begins, and everything else follows from it. Before John sees the terrors of the world, he sees that the one who holds the keys of death is the one who laid his hand on him and said, “Do not be afraid.”

Seven letters to seven churches

Chapters 2 and 3 hold seven short letters from the risen Jesus, to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea. Each says “I know…”, and five of them “I know your works”. Each describes Jesus in words drawn from the opening vision. Each ends with a promise “to everyone who overcomes”, and with the refrain, “Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”

The churches are not alike. Ephesus works hard and guards the truth but has let go of “the love you had in the beginning” (2:4). Smyrna is poor and persecuted, and is told, “Stay faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life” (2:10). Pergamum and Thyatira have made peace with idolatry. Sardis has a name for being alive, but is dead. Philadelphia has little strength but has kept Christ’s word. Laodicea is rich and satisfied and “lukewarm, neither hot nor cold” (3:16), and to that comfortable church Jesus speaks the most tender words of all:

Look: I am standing at the door, knocking. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and share a meal with them, and they with me.

— Revelation 3:20

Two dangers run through the letters: persecution from outside, and compromise from within. Some of the churches are in danger of being crushed; others are in danger of being too comfortable to notice that anything is wrong. The rest of the book is written for both.

The throne and the Lamb

In chapter 4 John sees “a door standing open” in heaven, and is taken up to see a throne, with someone seated on it, surrounded by a rainbow, by twenty-four elders and by four living creatures who never stop saying, “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, the Almighty, the one who was and who is and who is coming.” Before anything happens on earth, John is shown who is on the throne. The world is not out of control.

Then, in chapter 5, comes the turning point of the whole book. In God’s right hand is a scroll sealed with seven seals, and no one is worthy to open it. John weeps bitterly. One of the elders tells him to stop weeping:

Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop weeping! Look: the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome, so he can open the scroll and its seven seals.”

— Revelation 5:5

John turns to see the Lion, and sees instead a Lamb:

Then, at the center of the throne and the four living creatures, among the elders, I saw a Lamb standing, looking as though he had been slaughtered. He had seven horns and seven eyes; these are the seven spirits of God, sent out into all the earth.

— Revelation 5:6

This is the heart of Revelation. The Lion of Judah, the conquering King Israel longed for, has conquered as a slaughtered Lamb. God’s power to bring history to its goal is the power of the cross. From here on the book calls Jesus “the Lamb” nearly thirty times, and all heaven sings to him a new song: “at the cost of your blood you bought for God those from every tribe and language and people and nation” (5:9).

Seals, trumpets and bowls

The Lamb opens the seals, and a series of judgments begins: the four horsemen of conquest, war, famine and death; the cry of the martyrs under the altar, “how long”; the great earthquake; and at the seventh seal, silence in heaven “for about half an hour” (8:1). Then seven trumpets sound, and then seven bowls of God’s fury are poured out. Many of these plagues echo the plagues of Egypt, and the people of God who come through them sing “the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb” (15:3). Revelation is telling the story of a new exodus.

The three series are not simply one long timeline. Each seems to bring us to the edge of the end and then start again, more intense each time, as though the same reality were being shown from three angles. And between them come pauses, in which the people of God are shown safe. In chapter 7, before the winds of judgment blow, God’s servants are sealed on their foreheads. John hears their number, 144,000, from every tribe of Israel; then he turns and sees “a crowd so vast that no one could number it”, from every nation, standing before the throne. As with the Lion and the Lamb, what John hears and what he sees are, many readers think, the same people described two ways.

Numbers that mean

Revelation is full of numbers, and almost all of them are symbols. Seven is the number of completeness: seven churches, spirits, seals, trumpets, bowls. Twelve is the number of God’s people, the twelve tribes and the twelve apostles; twelve times twelve times a thousand is 144,000. Three and a half, half of seven, is the time of trouble, cut short: it appears as 1,260 days, as forty-two months, and as “a time, and times, and half a time”, a phrase from Daniel. A thousand is a great and complete number. Reading these as a calendar has led to much confusion; reading them as John’s first hearers would have done opens the book up.

The dragon, the beasts and Babylon

Chapters 12 to 18 pull back the curtain further, to show the conflict behind the conflicts. A woman clothed with the sun gives birth to a son who is to rule the nations, and a great red dragon waits to devour him. The child is caught up to God; there is war in heaven; and the dragon, “the serpent of old, the one called the devil and Satan, deceiver of the whole world” (12:9), is thrown down. He has lost, and knows his time is short. How do God’s people overcome him?

They have overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony; they did not hold their lives dear, even in the face of death.

— Revelation 12:11

Then the dragon calls up two beasts: one from the sea, a monstrous empire that blasphemes God and makes war on his people, and one from the land, with horns like a lamb’s and a voice like a dragon’s, which makes everyone worship the first. The beast is a grim parody of the Lamb: it too has a wound that was healed; it too is worshipped by every tribe and nation. Its mark, and its number, 666, have been fitted to countless names over the centuries. Irenaeus warned long ago that “many names can be found possessing the number mentioned”. Many scholars think John’s first readers would have heard in it the name of Nero, whose name in Hebrew letters adds up to 666; others take it as a symbol of a power that always falls short of seven. Either way, John’s point is less a puzzle than a warning: “Here is where God’s holy people need endurance and faith” (13:10).

And then there is Babylon, “Babylon the great, mother of prostitutes and of the earth’s abominations” (17:5), seated on seven mountains, drunk on the blood of God’s people, rich with the trade of the whole world. For John’s first hearers, a city on seven hills could only be Rome. But Babylon is more than one city. She is every power that seduces the world with wealth and luxury and is built on the suffering of others; the long list of her cargoes in chapter 18 ends with “slaves, human lives”. God’s word to his people is not to fight her but to leave her: “Leave her, my people, so that you have no part in her sins” (18:4).

The rider, the thousand years and the throne

When Babylon falls, heaven breaks into song: “Hallelujah! For the Lord God, the Almighty, has begun to reign” (19:6). The wedding of the Lamb has come. Heaven opens, and a rider on a white horse comes out, named Faithful and True, his robe dipped in blood, and “the name by which he is called is the Word of God” (19:13). His only weapon is the sword that comes from his mouth.

Chapter 20 tells of Satan bound for a thousand years, of martyrs who come to life and reign with Christ, of a last rebellion, and of the great white throne where the dead are judged. Few chapters of the Bible have been read in more ways. Some Christians, called premillennialists, believe Christ will return and then reign on earth for a thousand years; Irenaeus and Justin Martyr held a form of this view. Others, amillennialists, following Augustine in The City of God, take the thousand years as the present age of the church, between Christ’s first coming and his return. Still others, postmillennialists, expect a long age of the gospel’s triumph before he comes. All agree on the end: Christ returns, the dead are raised, evil is judged, and death itself is thrown into the lake of fire.

Everything new

And then the last vision, the most beautiful in the Bible:

Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; the first heaven and the first earth had gone, and the sea was no more. And the holy city, the new Jerusalem, I saw descending out of heaven from God, ready like a bride who has adorned herself for her husband.

— Revelation 21:1–2

The holy city does not rise from earth to heaven; it comes down from heaven to earth. God makes his home with human beings, and wipes every tear from their eyes. The one on the throne says, “See, I am making everything new!” (21:5). The city is a perfect cube, like the holy of holies in Solomon’s temple, and so “There was no temple to be seen in the city: its temple is the Lord God, the Almighty, and the Lamb” (21:22). Through it flows the river of the water of life, and beside it grows the tree of life, whose “leaves bring healing to the nations” (22:2).

The Bible that began in a garden ends in a garden-city. The tree of life, lost in Genesis, is given back. The curse is lifted: “Nothing accursed will be found there any longer” (22:3). And the thing every human heart was made for is given at last: “they will look upon his face” (22:4).

Four ways of reading

Christians have read Revelation in four broad ways, and most thoughtful readers draw something from more than one. Preterists read it chiefly as a message about John’s own time, the struggle of the early church with Rome. Historicists read it as a map of church history from the first century to the end. Futurists read most of it, from chapter 4 on, as describing events still to come, just before Christ’s return. Idealists read it as a picture of the struggle between God and evil in every age. Each has insight to offer, and each can be pressed too far. Whatever one’s view, the book’s message to every age is the same: Jesus is Lord, evil will not have the last word, and those who stay faithful will share his victory.

How to read Revelation

Read it aloud, as it was meant to be read; it takes about an hour and a quarter. Its shape is simple enough to hold: the vision of Christ and the seven letters (1–3); the throne and the Lamb (4–5); the seals, trumpets and bowls, with their pauses (6–16); the fall of Babylon (17–19:10); the final victory, the thousand years and the judgment (19:11–20:15); and the new creation (21–22).

Listen for the Old Testament. Revelation hardly quotes it directly, yet most of its verses allude to it: to Exodus, Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Zechariah and the Psalms. Listen for the songs, which come at every turning point and have filled the church’s hymnbooks. And listen for the seven blessings scattered through the book (1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7; 22:14). They show what the book is for. It is not written to make its readers anxious, but blessed.

About this translation

The text in this edition is the Open Word Bible, a new translation made directly from the Greek and given freely to the public domain. It is printed here at its Balanced level, which aims to be accurate and to read naturally aloud. A few of its choices in Revelation are worth knowing about before you begin.

“Affliction” and “overcomes.” Where older Bibles say “tribulation”, this translation says “affliction”, the same word John uses of the troubles he shares with his readers (1:9); so the “great tribulation” of 7:14 is here “the great affliction”. And it keeps “overcome” for the Greek word of victory, from the promises to the churches to the Lamb who overcomes the kings of the earth, so that a reader can follow the theme through the book.

Places where manuscripts differ. In 1:5 it reads that Christ “by his blood released us from our sins”; some later manuscripts have “washed”, a difference of one letter in Greek. In 22:14 it reads “How blessed are those who wash their robes!”, where the King James Version, following later manuscripts, has “do his commandments”. The number of the beast is 666; a few early witnesses read 616, as Irenaeus already knew.

Measures. The Open Word Bible lets a reader choose modern measures or the original ones. This edition prints the modern ones, so the holy city measures “about 1,400 miles” and its wall “about 216 feet”. In the Greek they are 12,000 stadia and 144 cubits, numbers built on twelve, and in Revelation that matters.

Numbering. The verse about the dragon standing on the seashore is 12:18 in some Bibles and the start of 13:1 in others. References here follow the King James numbering. And where the Greek says Christos, the Open Word Bible lets a reader choose “Christ” or “the Messiah”; this edition prints “Christ”.

For the reasoning behind every sentence of the translation, with the Greek beside it, see the Open Word Bible itself at openwordbible.org.

fields.title: Revelation 1
fields.body_html:
The revelation of Jesus Christ

This is the revelation of Jesus Christ. God gave it to him so that he would show his servants the things that must happen soon. He sent his angel to his servant John and through the angel made these things known. John has borne witness to all he saw, to the word of God and the testimony of Jesus Christ. How blessed is the one who reads the words of this prophecy aloud, and those who hear them and keep what is written here! The time is near. From John, to the seven churches in the province of Asia. Grace to you and peace from the one who is, who was, and who is coming; from the seven spirits that are before his throne; and from Jesus Christ, the witness who is faithful, the firstborn from among the dead, and the ruler over the kings of the earth.

To him who loves us and by his blood released us from our sins, and who made us a kingdom, priests in the service of his God and Father—to him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.

Look! He is coming with the clouds. Every eye will see him, those who pierced him among them, and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts in grief over him. Yes! Amen.

“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God—the one who is, who was, and who is coming, the Almighty.

One like a son of man among the lampstands

I, John, am your brother, and in Jesus I share with you the affliction, the kingdom, and the endurance. It was because of God’s word and the testimony of Jesus that I came to be on the island called Patmos. On the Lord’s day I came to be in the Spirit, and from behind me I heard a loud voice that sounded like a trumpet. It said, “Write in a scroll what you are seeing, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”

I turned around to see whose voice it was that spoke with me, and as I turned I saw seven lampstands made of gold. In the middle of the lampstands was one like a son of man. A long robe came down to his feet, and a gold sash was tied around his chest. His head and hair were white as wool is white, white as snow, and his eyes were like flaming fire. His feet were like fine bronze, fired as in a furnace, and his voice sounded like many waters. Seven stars were in his right hand, a sharp sword with two edges came out of his mouth, and his face was as bright as the sun when it shines with all its strength.

At the sight of him I fell down at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me and said, “Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last and the one who lives. I was dead, and see, I am alive for all the ages to come, and the keys of death and Hades are mine. So put in writing what you saw, what is, and what will come about after this. As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw in my right hand and the seven gold lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.”

fields.title: Revelation 2
fields.body_html:
To the church in Ephesus

To the angel of the church in Ephesus, write: “This is the message of the one who grips the seven stars in his right hand, who walks about among the seven lampstands of gold: I know your works, how hard you have labored and how you have endured. I know that you cannot put up with people who do evil. Those who call themselves apostles, though they are not, you put to the test and found to be false. You keep going. For my name’s sake you have carried heavy loads, and you have not grown tired. But here is my complaint against you: the love you had in the beginning, you have let go. So call to mind the height you have fallen from. Repent, and act as you did at the start. Otherwise I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand from where it stands, unless you repent. Yet there is this to your credit: you hate the things the Nicolaitans do, and so do I. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches. I will let everyone who overcomes eat from the tree of life that grows in God’s paradise.”

To the church in Smyrna

To the angel of the church in Smyrna, write: “This is the message of the first and the last, the one who was dead and came to life: I know your affliction and your poverty—though in fact you are rich—and the abuse you receive from those who claim to be Jews but are not. They are Satan’s synagogue. Have no fear of anything you are going to suffer. Look: some of you the devil is about to throw into prison, so that you will be tested, and you will face affliction for ten days. Stay faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches. The second death will never harm anyone who overcomes.”

To the church in Pergamum

To the angel of the church in Pergamum, write: “This is the message of the one who has the sharp sword with two edges: I know where you make your home: the place of Satan’s throne. Still you keep a firm grip on my name. Even in the days of Antipas, my witness and my faithful one, who was killed among you where Satan lives, you did not disown your faith in me. But I have a few complaints against you. You have people there who hold to what Balaam taught. He showed Balak how to set a trap for the Israelites, so that they would eat food offered to idols and commit sexual immorality. You also have, in the same way, people who cling to the Nicolaitans’ teaching. Repent, then. Otherwise I am coming to you soon, and I will wage war on them with the sword that comes from my mouth. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches. To everyone who overcomes I will give a share of the hidden manna. I will give each one a white stone too, and written on the stone is a new name that only the one who receives it knows.”

To the church in Thyatira

To the angel of the church in Thyatira, write: “This is the message of the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like fine bronze: I know your works—the love, the faith, the service, the endurance that are yours—and that your recent works outnumber your first ones. But I hold this against you: you put up with the woman Jezebel, the self-styled prophet. She teaches my servants and deceives them into sexual immorality and into eating food offered to idols. I gave her time to repent, and she is not willing to turn away from her sexual immorality. Look, I am laying her on a sickbed, and those who commit adultery with her I am throwing into great affliction, unless they repent of the things she does. Her children I will put to death, and all the churches will come to know that I search the inner self, mind and heart, and that I will give each of you what your works deserve. But to the rest of you in Thyatira, all who do not hold this teaching and have not learned the deep things of Satan, as they call them, I say this: I will lay no other burden on you. Just keep a firm grip on what you have until I come. To everyone who overcomes and keeps doing my works to the end I will give authority over the nations. They will shepherd the nations with a rod of iron, as clay pots are smashed to pieces, with the same authority I myself received from my Father. And to each of them I will give the morning star. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”

fields.title: Revelation 3
fields.body_html:
To the church in Sardis

To the angel of the church in Sardis, write: “This is the message of the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works. People speak of you as alive, but you are dead. Become watchful, and put strength into what remains and was on the point of dying, for I have found that your works are not complete before my God. Think back, then, to the way you received the message and heard it. Keep it, and repent. If you stay asleep, I will come like a thief, and you will never know the hour when I come against you. Still, you have a few people in Sardis who have not stained their clothes. They will walk with me dressed in white, for they deserve it. Everyone who overcomes will be clothed in this way, in white. I will never erase their name from the book of life. Before my Father and before his angels I will openly own their name. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”

To the church in Philadelphia

To the angel of the church in Philadelphia, write: “This is the message of the holy and true one, the one with the key of David: when he opens, no one will shut, and when he shuts, no one opens: I know your works. Look: I have opened a door for you, and no one can shut it. Your strength is small, yet you have kept my word, and you have not disowned my name. Look at what I will do with those from Satan’s synagogue, who claim to be Jews and are not, but lie: I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will learn that I have loved you. You have kept my call to endure, and so I in turn will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come over the whole world, to put the people of the earth to the test. I am coming soon. Keep a firm grip on what you have, so that no one takes your crown. I will make everyone who overcomes a pillar in the temple of my God, never again to go out of it. On them I will write the name of my God, and the name of my God’s city, the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”

To the church in Laodicea

To the angel of the church in Laodicea, write: “This is the message of the Amen, the witness who is faithful and true, the origin of God’s creation: I know your works: you are not cold, and you are not hot. If only you were one or the other, cold or hot! As it is, you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, and so I am about to spew you out of my mouth. You tell yourself, ‘I am rich. I have built up my wealth, and I lack nothing.’ You do not see that it is you who are wretched and to be pitied, poor and blind and naked. So here is my advice: buy from me gold that has been through the fire, and you will be rich; buy white garments and dress in them, and the shame of your nakedness will not be seen; and buy ointment for your eyes and put it on them, and you will see. I correct and train all whom I love. Be eager, then, and repent. Look: I am standing at the door, knocking. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and share a meal with them, and they with me. To everyone who overcomes I will give a place beside me on my throne, just as I overcame and took my seat beside my Father on his throne. Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”

fields.title: Revelation 4
fields.body_html:
The throne in heaven

After this I looked, and there in heaven was a door standing open. The voice I had heard at first, the one like a trumpet that spoke with me, said, “Come up here, and I will show you what must happen.” After this, at once I came to be in the Spirit, and I saw a throne standing in heaven, with someone seated on it. The one seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow that looked like emerald. Around the throne stood twenty-four other thrones, and on them sat twenty-four elders, dressed in white, with gold crowns on their heads. Lightning flashes out from the throne, with sounds and thunder. Before the throne seven torches of fire are burning, which are the seven spirits of God, and before it lies what looks like a sea of glass, like crystal.

And at the throne’s center and all around it were four living beings, full of eyes front and back. The first creature looked like a lion; the second looked like an ox; the third had a face like a human face; and the fourth looked like an eagle in flight. The four living creatures have six wings apiece and are full of eyes around and within. Without rest, day and night, they say: “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, the Almighty, the one who was and who is and who is coming.” Each time the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever, the twenty-four elders fall down before him and worship the one who lives forever and ever. They throw down their crowns in front of the throne, saying: “Our Lord and God, you are worthy to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, because you created all things: because you willed it, they existed and were created.”

fields.title: Revelation 5
fields.body_html:
The sealed scroll

In the right hand of the one seated on the throne I saw a scroll. It was written on the inside and on the back, and seven seals closed it. A strong angel was there too, and I heard him cry out with a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the scroll’s seals and open it?” No one at all, in heaven, on the earth, or beneath it, was able to open the scroll or look into it. I began to weep bitterly, since no one had been found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it. Then one of the elders said to me, “Stop weeping! Look: the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome, so he can open the scroll and its seven seals.”

The Lamb takes the scroll

Then, at the center of the throne and the four living creatures, among the elders, I saw a Lamb standing, looking as though he had been slaughtered. He had seven horns and seven eyes; these are the seven spirits of God, sent out into all the earth. He came and received the scroll out of the right hand of the one seated on the throne. As soon as he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders bowed low before the Lamb. Every one of them had a harp, and they held gold bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of God’s holy people. They sing a new song: “Worthy are you to receive the scroll and to break open its seals, for you were slaughtered, and at the cost of your blood you bought for God those from every tribe and language and people and nation. You made them a kingdom, and priests serving our God, and they reign on the earth.”

Then I looked, and I heard the voices of many angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. Their number was beyond counting: ten thousands of ten thousands, and thousands of thousands. With a loud voice they said, “Worthy is the Lamb who was slaughtered to receive power, wealth, wisdom, might, honor, glory, and blessing!” Then every created thing in heaven, on earth, under the earth and on the sea, all that they hold, I heard saying: “To the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might forever and ever!” The four living creatures said, “Amen!” And the elders fell down and worshiped.

fields.title: Revelation 6
fields.body_html:
The first four seals

I looked on as the Lamb broke open one of the seven seals. One of the four living creatures cried out with a voice like thunder, and I heard it say, “Come!” I looked, and I saw a white horse. The one who sat on it carried a bow. A crown was given to him, and out he went, winning victories and set on winning more.

The Lamb broke the second seal, and I heard the second living creature say, “Come!” Out came another horse, red as fire. The one riding it was permitted to take peace from the earth and to make people slaughter each other, and a great sword was put in his hand.

The Lamb broke the third seal, and I heard the third living creature say, “Come!” I looked, and there was a black horse, and the one who sat on it had a balance in his hand. And I heard what sounded like a voice among the four living creatures, saying: “A quart of wheat for a day’s wages, and three quarts of barley for a day’s wages, but do not damage the olive oil and the wine!”

The Lamb broke the fourth seal, and I heard the fourth living creature say, “Come!” I looked, and I saw a horse the sickly green of a corpse. Death was the name of the one who sat on it, and Hades went along with him. To them was given power over a quarter of the earth, to kill with the sword, with hunger, with deadly disease, and by the earth’s wild animals.

The fifth seal: the souls under the altar

When he opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slaughtered for the sake of the word of God and of the witness they held to. They cried out with a loud voice: “Holy and true Master, how long until you judge those who live on the earth and give justice for our blood?” A white robe was handed to each of them, and they were told to rest a short time more, until the number of their fellow servants and brothers and sisters was complete, those who were going to be killed as they had been.

The sixth seal: the great day

Then I saw him open the sixth seal, and a great earthquake struck. The sun went as black as sackcloth made of hair, the full moon became like blood, and the stars in the sky dropped to the earth, the way unripe figs drop from a fig tree when a gale shakes it. The sky was torn away like a scroll that rolls itself up, and every mountain and island was shifted out of its place. Then the earth’s kings and its high officials, its military commanders, its wealthy and its powerful, and every slave and every free person, went into hiding in the caves and the mountain crags. To the mountains and rocks they cry, “Fall on us! Cover us from the sight of the one seated on the throne, and from the Lamb’s wrath! For the great day of their wrath is here, and who is able to stand?”

fields.title: Revelation 7
fields.body_html:
God’s servants are sealed

Next I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth. They were holding back the earth’s four winds, so that no wind could blow on land or sea or on any tree. I saw yet another angel, coming up from where the sun rises and carrying the seal of the living God. In a loud voice he called to the four angels who had been allowed to harm the earth and the sea: “Hold off from harming the earth, the sea, and the trees until we have marked the servants of our God with a seal on their foreheads.”

And I heard how many were sealed: 144,000, sealed from every tribe of the Israelites. From the tribe of Judah, 12,000 were sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, 12,000; from the tribe of Gad, 12,000; from the tribe of Asher, 12,000; from the tribe of Naphtali, 12,000; from the tribe of Manasseh, 12,000; from the tribe of Simeon, 12,000; from the tribe of Levi, 12,000; from the tribe of Issachar, 12,000; from the tribe of Zebulun, 12,000; from the tribe of Joseph, 12,000; and from the tribe of Benjamin, 12,000 were sealed.

A crowd from every nation

After this I looked, and I saw a crowd so vast that no one could number it. They came from every nation and from all tribes and peoples and languages, and they stood before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands. With a loud voice they cry out: “To our God, seated on the throne, and to the Lamb, salvation belongs!” Every angel stood in a circle around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures, and they threw themselves face down before the throne and worshiped God. “Amen!” they said. “Blessing and glory, wisdom and thanksgiving, honor and power and might be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”

One of the elders turned to me with a question: “Those clothed in the white robes, who are they, and from where have they come?” I answered, “Sir, you are the one who knows.” He said to me, “These are the ones who are coming out of the great affliction. They have washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb and made them white. For this reason they stand before God’s throne and serve him day and night in his temple, and the one who sits on the throne will spread his tent over them. No more will they go hungry, no more will they be thirsty; the sun will not strike them, nor any burning heat. For the Lamb in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and guide them to springs of the water of life, and every tear God will wipe from their eyes.”

fields.title: Revelation 8
fields.body_html:
The seventh seal and the golden censer

When he broke the seventh seal, heaven fell silent for about half an hour. And I saw the seven angels who stand in God’s presence; they were given seven trumpets.

Then another angel came, holding a gold censer, and took his place at the altar. Much incense was handed to him, so that he could add it to the prayers of all God’s holy people on the gold altar before the throne. The smoke of the incense rose with the prayers of God’s holy people from the angel’s hand before God. The angel then took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and flung it onto the earth. Thunder crashed, there were loud sounds and lightning, and the earth shook.

The first four trumpets

Then the seven angels holding the seven trumpets made ready to blow them.

When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire, mixed with blood, were flung down on the earth. A third of the land was burned up, and a third of the trees, and every green blade of grass.

Then the second angel blew his trumpet. What looked like a great mountain on fire was hurled into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood. Of the creatures living in the sea a third died, and of the ships a third were wrecked.

The third angel blew his trumpet, and down from the sky came a huge star, burning like a torch. It landed on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water. The star’s name is Wormwood. A third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many people died from the water, because it had been made bitter.

Then the fourth angel blew his trumpet. A blow fell on a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, and a third of their light was darkened: for a third of the day nothing shone, and so too for the night.

Then I looked, and I heard an eagle flying high overhead call out in a loud voice: “Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, at the blasts of the trumpets that the three remaining angels are about to blow!”

fields.title: Revelation 9
fields.body_html:
The fifth trumpet: locusts from the abyss

When the fifth angel blew his trumpet, I saw a star that had fallen from the sky to the earth, and to him was given the key to the shaft that leads down into the abyss. He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke rose from it like smoke from a huge furnace; the sun and the air grew dark with the smoke from the shaft. From the smoke locusts swarmed out over the earth, and they were given the kind of power scorpions have. Their orders were to leave alone the earth’s grass, every green plant, and every tree, and to harm only the people without the seal of God on their foreheads. Killing them was not permitted; the locusts could only torment them for five months, and the pain they caused was like the pain of a scorpion’s sting on a person. During those days people will search for death, but it will not be found; they will want to die, and death will keep fleeing from them.

In shape the locusts were like horses made ready for war. They had what looked like gold crowns on their heads, and their faces were like the faces of human beings. Their hair was like a woman’s hair, their teeth like a lion’s. Their chests were armored as if with iron breastplates, and their wings made a noise like chariots and many horses charging into battle. Like scorpions they have tails with stings, and it is with their tails that they have power to harm people for five months. Over them they have a king, the angel of the abyss. In Hebrew his name is Abaddon, and in Greek he is called Apollyon.

The first woe is over. Look: two woes are still to come after this.

The sixth trumpet: the army from the Euphrates

Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a single voice from the horns of the gold altar that stands before God. It said to the sixth angel, who held the trumpet, “Set free the four angels who are held bound beside the great river, the Euphrates.” The four angels were set loose. They had been made ready for that hour, that day, month, and year, to kill a third of humankind. Their mounted armies numbered 200,000,000; I heard the count. This is how I saw the horses and their riders in my vision. The riders wore breastplates the colors of fire, of dark blue hyacinth, and of yellow sulfur. The horses’ heads were like lions’ heads, and fire, smoke, and sulfur poured from their mouths. These three plagues, the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur coming out of their mouths, killed a third of humankind. It is in their mouths that the horses’ power lies, and in their tails too, for their tails are like snakes with heads, and with these they wound.

Yet the rest of humankind, who survived these plagues, did not repent and turn from the things their own hands had made: they went on worshiping demons, and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood that have no power to see or hear or walk. There was no repentance for their murders or their sorcery, for their sexual immorality or their stealing.

fields.title: Revelation 10
fields.body_html:
The angel and the little scroll

Then another mighty angel came into view, coming down from heaven. A cloud was his clothing, and the rainbow crowned his head; his face shone like the sun, his legs were like pillars of fire, and he held a small scroll, open, in his hand. Planting his right foot on the sea and his left on the land, he called out in a great voice, as a lion roars. When he had called out, the seven thunders spoke with their voices. As soon as the seven thunders had spoken, I was ready to write, but a voice from heaven told me, “Seal up the words of the seven thunders; do not write them down.” The angel I had seen standing on sea and land lifted his right hand toward heaven and took an oath by the one who lives forever and ever, the maker of heaven and everything in it, of the earth and everything in it, and of the sea and everything in it, that there would be no more delay. Instead, when the days come for the seventh angel’s trumpet, when he is about to blow it, God’s mystery will reach its completion, the good news he announced to his servants the prophets.

The voice from heaven that I had heard spoke with me once again. “Go,” it said, “and take the scroll lying open in the hand of the angel who stands on sea and land.” I went over to the angel and told him to hand me the little scroll. “Take it,” he told me, “and eat it up. It will make your stomach bitter, though in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.” I took the little scroll out of the angel’s hand and ate it up. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it my stomach became bitter.

Then they said to me, “Once more you must prophesy, concerning many peoples and nations and languages and kings.”

fields.title: Revelation 11
fields.body_html:
The two witnesses

I was given a measuring rod like a staff and told, “Get up and measure God’s temple and the altar, and count those who worship there. But leave out the court outside the temple; do not measure it, for it has been handed over to the nations, and they will tread the holy city underfoot for forty-two months. I will give power to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, dressed in sackcloth.”

These two are the olive trees and the lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth. Should anyone want to hurt them, fire comes out of their mouths and burns up their enemies. Whoever wants to hurt them is bound to be killed like this. It is in their power to close the sky, so that no rain falls in the days of their prophecy; they also have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and power to strike the earth with every kind of plague whenever they choose.

When they have completed their testimony, the beast that rises from the abyss will wage war against them, overpower them, and kill them. Their bodies will lie in the open street of the great city, which in a prophetic sense is called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord too was crucified. People from among the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations look on their bodies for three and a half days and will not let them be laid in a tomb. Those who live on the earth rejoice over their death and make merry; they will exchange gifts, because these two prophets had tormented the people of the earth.

After the three and a half days, though, the breath of life came into them from God; they rose to their feet, and those watching were seized by great fear. A great voice from heaven called to them, “Come up here!” They heard it, and up they went into heaven in the cloud, with their enemies watching them. In that same hour a great earthquake struck, a tenth of the city fell, and the quake killed 7,000 people. The rest were filled with fear and gave glory to the God of heaven.

The second woe is over. Look: the third woe is coming soon.

The seventh trumpet

Then the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and loud voices in heaven said: “The rule over the world now belongs to our Lord and to his Christ, and he will reign forever and ever.”

Then the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones in God’s presence threw themselves face down and worshiped God. “Lord God, the Almighty,” they said, “the one who is and who was, we thank you, for you have taken your great power into your hands and begun your reign. The nations raged, but your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, for your servants the prophets to be rewarded, and your holy people, and all who fear your name, small and great, and the time to destroy those who destroy the earth.”

God’s temple in heaven was thrown open, and inside it the ark of his covenant appeared. Lightning flashed; there were loud sounds and thunder, an earthquake, and huge hail.

fields.title: Revelation 12
fields.body_html:
The woman and the dragon

A great sign was seen in the sky: a woman wearing the sun as her clothing, the moon beneath her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars. She was with child, and she cried out in labor, in agony to give birth. And another sign was seen in the sky: look, a great dragon, red as fire, with seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven royal crowns. With his tail he drags away a third of the stars of heaven, and he threw them down to the earth. Before the woman who was about to give birth the dragon stood waiting, ready to devour her child the moment the child was born. She bore a son, a boy, the one who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up to God, to his throne. As for the woman, she fled into the wilderness. There God has a place ready for her, where she is to be fed for 1,260 days.

War in heaven

And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels went to battle against the dragon. The dragon and his angels fought back, but he was not strong enough, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven. Down went the great dragon, cast out: the serpent of old, the one called the devil and Satan, deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down along with him.

I heard a loud voice in heaven: “The time has come! Salvation is here, and power, and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of his Christ; for the one who accused our brothers and sisters, accusing them day and night before our God, has been cast out. They have overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony; they did not hold their lives dear, even in the face of death. So rejoice, you heavens, and all who live in them! Woe to earth and sea, because the devil has gone down to you full of fury, knowing that the time left to him is short.”

The dragon pursues the woman

Seeing that he had been thrown down to the earth, the dragon hunted the woman who had borne the boy. The woman was given the two wings of the great eagle to fly to her place in the wilderness, where she is cared for, away from the serpent, for a time, and times, and half a time. Then out of his mouth the serpent poured water after the woman, like a river, to have her carried off by the flood. But the earth came to the woman’s rescue: it opened its mouth and swallowed the river the dragon had poured from his mouth. In his fury against the woman the dragon went off to make war on the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus.

fields.title: Revelation 13
fields.body_html:
The beast from the sea

And the dragon took his stand on the sand of the seashore.

Then I saw a beast rising out of the sea. It had ten horns and seven heads, ten royal crowns on its horns, and on its heads names that blasphemed God. The beast I saw was like a leopard; its feet were like a bear’s, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion. The dragon handed over to it his power, his throne, and great authority. One of its heads looked as though it had been slaughtered and killed, but its deadly wound had been healed. In amazement the whole earth went after the beast. They worshiped the dragon, since he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast as well, saying, “Who is equal to the beast? Who could fight a war against it?” It was allowed a mouth that spoke boastful words and blasphemies, and it was given authority to act for forty-two months. Its mouth opened in blasphemies against God, insulting his name and his dwelling, those whose home is in heaven. It was allowed to make war on God’s holy people and to overcome them; and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation. All who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written, since the world was founded, in the book of life belonging to the Lamb who was slaughtered.

If anyone has ears, let them listen. Whoever is bound for captivity goes into captivity; whoever is to die by the sword must die by the sword. Here is where God’s holy people need endurance and faith.

The beast from the earth

I saw yet another beast coming up from the land. Its two horns were like a lamb’s, yet its voice was the voice of a dragon. All the authority of the first beast it puts to use, acting in its presence. It forces the earth and its people to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed. It performs great signs, even bringing fire down from the sky to the earth in front of everyone. It leads astray the people of the earth with the signs it was allowed to do in the beast’s presence, and it tells them to make an image for the beast that had the sword-wound and yet came back to life. It was permitted to give life-breath to the image of the beast, so that the image could even speak, and could have put to death all who refused to worship it. It makes everyone, the lowly and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slave, take a mark on the right hand or on the forehead. No one may buy or sell except those who have the mark: the name of the beast or the number that stands for its name. Here wisdom is needed. Whoever has understanding should count up the number of the beast, for it is a human number. Its number is 666.

fields.title: Revelation 14
fields.body_html:
The Lamb and the 144,000

I looked, and I saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion. With him stood 144,000 people, whose foreheads bore his name and the name of his Father. From heaven I heard a sound like the voice of many waters and of great thunder, and the sound was that of harpists playing on their harps. Before the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders they sing what seems a new song, a song no one could learn except the 144,000 bought out of the earth. These have kept themselves from being defiled with women; they are virgins. They are the followers of the Lamb, going wherever he goes. From among humankind they were bought as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb, and no lie was found in what they said; they are without blemish.

Three angels

I saw another angel too, flying high in the sky, who carried an eternal gospel to proclaim to the people who live on the earth, to every nation, tribe, language, and people. In a loud voice he cried, “Stand in awe of God and give him glory, for the hour has come when he will judge. Worship the maker of heaven and earth, of the sea and the springs of water.”

Another angel, a second one, came after him and said, “Babylon the great has fallen, has fallen! She made all the nations drink the wine of her raging immorality.”

A third angel followed them, calling out in a loud voice: “If anyone worships the beast and its image, and takes its mark on the forehead or the hand, they will also drink the wine of God’s fury, unwatered, mixed in the cup of his anger, and will suffer torment in fire and sulfur before the holy angels and before the Lamb. Forever and ever the smoke of their torment goes up; day and night they have no rest, the worshipers of the beast and its image, and all who take the mark of its name.”

This is where God’s holy people need endurance, those who keep God’s commandments and hold to their faith in Jesus.

A voice from heaven spoke to me: “Write: From now on, how blessed are the dead who die in the Lord!” “Indeed,” the Spirit says, “let them rest from their toil, for what they have done goes with them.”

The harvest of the earth

Then I saw a white cloud, and on it sat one like a son of man. A gold crown was on his head, and in his hand a sharp sickle. Out of the temple came another angel, crying aloud to the one seated on the cloud, “Swing your sickle and gather the harvest! The hour for reaping is here; the earth’s harvest is dry and ready.” The one on the cloud swept his sickle across the earth, and the earth’s harvest was gathered in.

Then from the temple in heaven came yet another angel, also holding a sharp sickle. And another angel came from the altar, the angel with power over the fire. In a great voice he called to the one holding the sharp sickle, “Swing your sharp sickle and cut the bunches from the vine of the earth, for its grapes are at their ripest.” The angel swept his sickle across the earth, cut the earth’s vintage, and flung it into the winepress of God’s fury, the great winepress. Outside the city the winepress was trodden, and out of it came blood, up to the horses’ bridles, for about 180 miles.

fields.title: Revelation 15
fields.body_html:
Seven angels with the last plagues

Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and astonishing: seven angels with seven plagues, the last plagues, for with them God’s wrath is brought to an end.

I saw something like a sea of glass with fire mingled in it. By the glassy sea stood those who had overcome the beast, its image, and the number of its name, and they held harps of God. They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb: “How great and wonderful are your works, Lord God, the Almighty! Your ways are just and true, King of the ages! Lord, who will not fear and glorify your name? Only you are holy. Every nation will come and worship in your presence, because your acts of justice are now plain for all to see.”

Then I looked, and in heaven the temple, the tent of witness, stood open. From the temple the seven angels who held the seven plagues came out, robed in pure linen that shone, with gold sashes bound around their chests. One of the four living creatures handed the seven angels seven gold bowls, full to the brim with the fury of the God who lives forever and ever. Smoke from God’s glory and from his power filled the temple, and no one was able to enter it until the seven angels’ seven plagues were finished.

fields.title: Revelation 16
fields.body_html:
The seven bowls of God’s fury

I heard a great voice speak from the temple to the seven angels: “Go and empty the seven bowls of God’s fury onto the earth.”

The first angel went off and emptied his bowl on the earth, and foul, painful sores came on the people who bore the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.

When the second angel emptied his bowl into the sea, it became like the blood of a corpse, and everything that lived in the sea died.

The third angel emptied his bowl into the rivers and springs, and they turned to blood. Then I heard the angel of the waters say: “Just are you, the one who is and who was, the Holy One, for you have judged in this way. Because they poured out the blood of your holy people and prophets, blood is what you have given them to drink. It is what they have earned.” Then I heard the altar reply, “Yes, Lord God, the Almighty: your judgments are true and right.”

When the fourth angel emptied his bowl on the sun, it was given power to burn people with fire. Burned by the fierce heat, people blasphemed the name of the God who had power over these plagues; they would not repent and give him glory.

Then the fifth angel emptied his bowl over the beast’s throne, and darkness fell on its kingdom. In their anguish people chewed their tongues, and they blasphemed the God of heaven for their pains and their sores; yet they did not turn from their deeds.

When the sixth angel emptied his bowl on the great river, the Euphrates, its water was dried up so that a road would be ready for the kings from the sunrise. And out of the dragon’s mouth, the beast’s mouth, and the false prophet’s mouth I saw three unclean spirits come, like frogs. These are spirits of demons, doing signs, and they go out to the kings of all the world to assemble them for war on the great day of God, the Almighty. “Look, I come like a thief! How blessed is anyone who keeps watch and holds on to their clothes, and so will not walk about naked with their shame on view!” And the spirits brought the kings together at the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.

When the seventh angel emptied his bowl into the air, a great voice came out of the temple, from the throne: “It is done!” Lightning, loud sounds, and thunder followed, and an earthquake struck so violent that nothing like it had ever happened since human beings first lived on the earth. The great city was torn into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. Babylon the great was not forgotten before God: he made her drink the cup of the wine of his raging anger. Every island ran away, and the mountains were found no more. Hailstones weighing about seventy-five pounds each came down out of the sky on people, and they blasphemed God over the plague of hail, because the plague of it was very severe.

fields.title: Revelation 17
fields.body_html:
The prostitute on the beast

Then one of the seven angels who held the seven bowls came and spoke to me. “Come,” he said, “I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute, who is seated on many waters. With her the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and the people of the earth got drunk on the wine of her immorality.” In the Spirit he took me away to a wilderness. I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast. The beast was full of names that blasphemed God, and it had seven heads and ten horns. The woman wore purple and scarlet, and gold, precious stones, and pearls adorned her. She held a gold cup in her hand, brimming with abominations and with the uncleanness of her immorality. On her forehead was written a name, a mystery: “Babylon the great, mother of prostitutes and of the earth’s abominations.” And I saw the woman drunk on the blood of God’s holy people and on the blood of Jesus’s witnesses.

The sight of her filled me with great amazement. But the angel said to me, “Why are you amazed? Let me tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast with the seven heads and ten horns that carries her. The beast that you saw existed once and exists no longer; it is going to rise out of the abyss, and it goes on to destruction. The people of the earth, those whose names have not been written in the book of life since the world was founded, will marvel to see the beast, for it was, and is not, and will be present again.

Here a wise mind is needed. The seven heads are seven mountains, and the woman is seated on them. They are also seven kings. Five of them have fallen; one is now; the other is still to come, and when he does, he must remain only briefly. And the beast that was and is not is an eighth king, and yet it belongs to the seven, and it is on its way to destruction. As for the ten horns you saw, they are ten kings who have no kingdom yet; but together with the beast they receive royal authority for one hour. They are of one mind, and they hand over their power and authority to the beast. They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with him are the called, the chosen, the faithful.”

He went on: “The waters you saw, on which the prostitute sits, are peoples and crowds, nations and languages. The ten horns and the beast that you saw will turn against the prostitute in hatred, leave her ruined and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her up with fire. It is God who has moved their hearts to do what he intends: to act with one mind and to hand their kingdom over to the beast, until God’s words have been fulfilled. The woman you saw is the great city, the one that reigns over the kings of the earth.”

fields.title: Revelation 18
fields.body_html:
The fall of Babylon

After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven. He had great authority, and the earth shone with his glory. He shouted with a mighty voice: “Babylon the great has fallen, has fallen! She has become a home for demons, a lair for every unclean spirit, a lair for every unclean bird, a lair for every unclean and hateful beast. Through the wine of her raging immorality all the nations have fallen; the kings of the earth committed immorality with her, and the earth’s merchants grew rich from her extravagant luxury.”

Come out of her, my people

Then I heard another voice from heaven: “Leave her, my people, so that you have no part in her sins and do not suffer any of her plagues. For her sins have stacked up as high as heaven, and God has not forgotten her crimes. Treat her as she treated others; repay her twice over for her deeds; mix her a double draught in the very cup she mixed. In proportion to the glory she gave herself and the luxury she lived in, give her torment and mourning. In her heart she keeps saying, ‘Here I sit, a queen; I am not a widow, and mourning I will never see.’ So her plagues will strike in one day, death, grief, and famine, and fire will burn her up; for the Lord God who has judged her is strong.”

The earth’s kings, who shared her immorality and her luxury, will weep and beat their breasts over her as they watch the smoke rise from her burning. Keeping far away for fear of her torment, they will say, “Woe, woe, great city, Babylon, city of strength! In a single hour your judgment has come.”

The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their goods any more: goods of gold, silver, precious stones, and pearls; fine linen, purple, silk, and scarlet; all kinds of citron wood, and all sorts of objects of ivory, costly wood, bronze, iron, and marble; cinnamon and spice, incense, myrrh, and frankincense; wine and olive oil, fine flour and wheat; cattle and sheep; horses and carriages; and slaves, human lives. The harvest of all that your heart desired has left you, and everything rich and dazzling is lost to you; no one will ever find it again. Those who dealt in these things and were made rich by her will keep their distance in fear of her torment, weeping and grieving: “Woe, woe for the great city, which wore fine linen, purple, and scarlet, and was decked with gold, jewels, and pearls! So much wealth, and in one hour it is ruined!”

Every helmsman, every traveler by sea, the sailors and all who work on the sea kept their distance and shouted as they looked at the smoke of her burning: “What city was like the great city?” Throwing dust on their heads, weeping and mourning, they cried: “Woe, woe for the great city! Her wealth made rich everyone who owned a ship at sea, and in one hour she has been laid waste.”

Celebrate her fall, heaven, and you holy people, apostles, and prophets! God has taken up your case against her and judged it.

A strong angel picked up a stone like a huge millstone and flung it into the sea. “Like this,” he said, “violently, Babylon the great city will be hurled down, and no one will find her any more. No more will the music of harpists and singers, of flute players and trumpeters, be heard in you; no craftsman of any trade will be found in you again; the sound of the millstone will be heard in you no more; the light of a lamp will shine in you no more; the voices of bridegroom and bride will be heard in you no more. For your merchants were the great ones of the earth, and by your sorcery all the nations were led astray. The blood of prophets and of God’s holy people was found in her, the blood of all who have been slaughtered on the earth.”

fields.title: Revelation 19
fields.body_html:
Hallelujah in heaven

Then I heard something like the loud voice of a huge crowd in heaven: “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God, whose judgments are true and right. He has passed judgment on the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her immorality, and from her hand he has required the blood of his servants.” Again they said, “Hallelujah! Smoke rises from her forever and ever.” The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures bowed down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying: “Amen! Hallelujah!”

From the throne a voice called out: “Praise our God, all his servants and all who fear him, the lowly and the great!” And I heard something like the voice of a vast crowd, like the roar of many waters and the crash of mighty thunder: “Hallelujah! For the Lord God, the Almighty, has begun to reign. Let us be glad and rejoice greatly and give him the glory, for the Lamb’s wedding has come, and his bride has made herself ready. To her it has been granted to dress in fine linen, shining and pure.” The fine linen is the just deeds of God’s holy people.

He told me, “Write: How blessed are those who have been called to the Lamb’s wedding feast!” He also told me, “These are the true words of God.” Then I threw myself down at his feet to worship him. “Do not!” he said. “I am only a fellow servant with you and with your brothers and sisters who keep the testimony of Jesus. Give your worship to God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”

The rider on the white horse

Heaven opened before my eyes, and I saw a white horse. The one who sat on it is named Faithful and True; in righteousness he judges and goes to war. Like a flame of fire are his eyes, and many royal crowns are on his head. A name is written on him that only he knows. The robe he wears has been dipped in blood, and the name by which he is called is the Word of God. Behind him rode the armies that are in heaven, on white horses, clothed in pure white linen. From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike the nations. He will shepherd them with a rod of iron, and he treads the winepress of the wine of the furious wrath of God, the Almighty. On his robe and on his thigh is written a name: King of kings and Lord of lords.

Next I saw an angel standing in the sun. In a great voice he called to all the birds that fly high in the sky: “Come and gather for the great supper God is giving, to feed on the flesh of kings, of commanders, of the powerful, on the flesh of horses and of those who ride them, on the flesh of everyone, free and slave, lowly and great.” I saw the beast, and with it the kings of the earth and their armies, assembled to fight the one who sits on the horse and his army. But the beast was seized, together with the false prophet who had worked signs in its presence and had used them to deceive those who took the beast’s mark and bowed down to its image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of fire, burning with sulfur. The others were put to death by the sword of the one on the horse, the sword that came out of his mouth, and all the birds ate their fill of their flesh.

fields.title: Revelation 20
fields.body_html:
The thousand years

Then I saw an angel come down from heaven with the key to the abyss and a heavy chain in his hand. He took hold of the dragon, the serpent of old, who is the devil and Satan, and chained him up for a thousand years. Into the abyss he threw him, shutting it and setting a seal over him, so that he would deceive the nations no more until the thousand years were over. After that he must be let loose for a short time.

I saw thrones, and people seated on them who were given the right to judge. I saw too the souls of those beheaded for holding to the testimony of Jesus and the word of God, those who had refused to worship the beast or its image and had not let its mark be put on forehead or hand. They came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years. The other dead did not live again until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is anyone who has a share in the first resurrection! Over such people the second death has no power; they will serve as priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him a thousand years.

Once the thousand years are completed, Satan will be freed from his prison and will go out to deceive the nations at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, and to muster them for war, countless as the sand of the sea. Up they came across the whole width of the earth and encircled the camp of God’s holy people and the beloved city. Then fire fell from heaven and burned them up. Then the devil, their deceiver, was cast into the lake of fire and sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet are as well; and day and night, forever and ever, they will suffer torment.

The great white throne

Next I saw a great white throne, and the one who sat on it; from his face earth and sky ran away, and no place could be found for them. I saw the dead, the great and the lowly, standing in front of the throne. Books were opened, and so was another book, the book of life, and the dead were judged on the basis of what the books recorded, according to their deeds. The sea handed over its dead, and Death and Hades handed over theirs, and they were judged, every one of them, by their works. Then Death and Hades themselves were cast into the lake of fire. The lake of fire is the second death. And whoever was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.

fields.title: Revelation 21
fields.body_html:
A new heaven and a new earth

Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; the first heaven and the first earth had gone, and the sea was no more. And the holy city, the new Jerusalem, I saw descending out of heaven from God, ready like a bride who has adorned herself for her husband. Then I heard a loud voice from the throne: “See, God’s dwelling is with human beings! He will make his home with them, and they will be his peoples; God himself will be with them. Every tear he will wipe from their eyes. Death will be no more, and no more mourning, no crying, no pain. The former things have gone.”

And the one who sits on the throne said, “See, I am making everything new!” Then he said, “Write it down, because these words can be trusted, and they are true.” He said to me, “It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To anyone who is thirsty I will give water from the spring of life, free of charge. Whoever overcomes will inherit these things; I will be that person’s God, and that person will be my child. But as for the cowardly, the faithless, the vile, the murderers, the sexually immoral, those who practice sorcery, the idolaters, and all liars, their share is in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur. This is the second death.”

The new Jerusalem

One of the seven angels, those who had held the seven bowls brimming with the seven last plagues, came and talked with me. “Come,” he said, “I will show you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.” He took me away in the Spirit to a mountain, vast and high, and showed me Jerusalem, the holy city, descending out of heaven from God, radiant with the glory of God. It shone like the costliest of stones, like jasper, clear as crystal. Around it ran a wall, great and high, with twelve gates. Twelve angels stood at the gates, and names were inscribed on them, the names of the twelve tribes of the Israelites. Three gates faced east, three north, three south, and three west. Twelve foundation stones held up the city’s wall, and on them were the twelve names of the Lamb’s twelve apostles.

The one speaking with me held a golden reed for measuring, to take the measurements of the city, its gates, and its wall. The city is built as a square; its length is the same as its width. He measured the city with the reed: about 1,400 miles. Its length, its width, and its height are the same. He measured its wall too: about 216 feet by human measure, which the angel was using. The wall was made of jasper, and the city itself was pure gold, clear like glass. Every kind of precious stone adorned the foundations of the city wall: the first was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald, the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. Each of the twelve gates was a pearl: every gate was cut from one single pearl. And the city’s broad street was of pure gold, transparent as glass.

There was no temple to be seen in the city: its temple is the Lord God, the Almighty, and the Lamb. Neither sun nor moon is needed to give the city light; God’s glory lights it up, and its lamp is the Lamb. By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth bring their glory.
